chanting.title: Before chanting
chanting.body: Wash your hands and rinse your mouth. Light incense, stand upright, join your palms and recite “Namo Shakyamuni Buddha” three times.

chanting.title: While chanting
chanting.body: Pronounce each word clearly and keep pace with the wooden fish, with your mind fully on the words. Steadiness matters more than speed.

chanting.title: Recitation
chanting.body: Recite aloud, silently, or with moving lips. One phrase per breath, listening clearly to each phrase.

chanting.title: Dedication
chanting.body: When finished, dedicate the merit to your parents, loved ones and all beings.

meditation.title: Posture
meditation.body: Sit cross-legged or on a chair, back naturally straight, shoulders relaxed, hands resting in your lap.

meditation.title: Breathing
meditation.body: Breathe through the nose, slowly and gently. Follow each breath; you may count from one to ten and start again.

meditation.title: Mind
meditation.body: When thoughts arise, notice them without following or resisting, and gently return to the breath.

meditation.title: Ending
meditation.body: At the closing bell, rub your palms, face and legs before slowly standing up.

woodenFish.title: The wooden fish
woodenFish.body: It keeps the rhythm of chanting: one strike per word or phrase, helping everyone chant together with a settled mind.

woodenFish.title: The mala
woodenFish.body: 108 beads stand for 108 afflictions. Move one bead per recitation; at the end of a round, turn back rather than passing the guru bead.

woodenFish.title: Try it here
woodenFish.body: Tap the wooden fish or a bead, or press Space. Turn on auto rhythm to keep time while chanting.

prayers.title: Prayers for peace
prayers.body: For the living to be safe, healthy and free from misfortune — often at the new year, on full and new moon days, or when loved ones are ill.

prayers.title: Prayers for the departed
prayers.body: For the departed to be liberated and reborn in a peaceful realm — often during the 49 days after death, on anniversaries and during Ullambana.

prayers.title: The heart of prayer
prayers.body: A prayer is precious for its sincerity, not its words. Doing good deeds, eating vegetarian and releasing life in dedication make the merit greater.
